body: The a11y assertions that run inside the existing test suites: every suite that holds them now spawns viola through the tied support, and integration and E2E stayed green with the tie in place.

The rule that a11y failures are nextest failures and a11y cases run in the coverage suite: the selection counts moved (integration 505 to 509, E2E 348 to 369) by the new killed-test and stamp witnesses, none of them an a11y case.
Zero flakiness with no retries: a CI profile kill timeout override (the stamped-home 20 s kill) now also covers the new killed-test binary; a row holding that bound or that override list is touched.
The CI test gate that allows no skips and requires coverage: new test binaries joined the gated suites, none skipped.
The TUI boundary driver and the outer-PTY boundary tests: an outer-PTY wrapper a test spawns is now tied and witnessed gone when its test is killed; the boundary assertions themselves are unchanged.
Boundary tests sequenced on records: the new witnesses read a pid report the victim writes, not screen content.
Time bounds fall on the driver only: the new gone-within wait bounds the test driver, never the human.
No separate a11y driver or suite value: the new binaries are process-hygiene witnesses inside the existing integration and E2E suites, not an a11y driver.
Live readings never gate: no live claude start was made; the harness session tie and smoke ran against the fake agent.

The plain-mode and refusal literal pins (fixed CLI strings pinned by literal, refusal layout held by literal pins): the suites holding them had only their viola spawn moved to the tied form; no literal changed.
The CLI output contracts themselves: no step line, waiting line, refusal unable/hint pair, exit code, --json document, fault body or code word changed.
Colour and SGR decisions (word beside every SGR, amber, bold, dim on stale rows, no colour on failure words) and NAME truncation: no output rendering changed.
Screen-reader targets, setups and the manual Orca and keyboard passes: nothing changed in them.
The absences (web or graphical frontend, touch surface, rendered page, internationalization, user time limit): no capability added or removed.
The CI supply-chain red (a chrono advisory) is not an a11y gate and is not mended in this session; the a11y GitHub Actions workflow rows are not moved by it.
TUI passthrough contracts (human keystrokes, viola terminal bytes, focus/mouse/resize, vendor content, feed panic) and the wheel decisions: no runtime behaviour of the wrapper changed.

The session ties every long-lived viola child a root test spawns to the test's spawning thread: a parent-death SIGKILL, plus an exit when the recorded parent is already gone, so a killed or panicked test leaves no booted wrapper or fake agent running.
An in-test harness session's supervisor and its stamping viola verify are tied the same way; the viola-harness CLI boot keeps its supervisor untied and behaves as before. Two other in-test viola-e2e boots also stay untied, and that gap is left to the route.
The shared verify stamp used by test homes now counts only when it holds a completion file and the ledger stamps file. A hollow stamp, for example one a CI cache restore left without its files, is left as found, and a next-generation stamp dir is built beside it. Nothing is removed.
A census test now holds the count of root viola spawns outside the tie helper at 0. Before, there were 45 such sites, one more than research had counted.
Two test-only self-spawn environment markers are added outside the VIOLA_ namespace. No product crate, wire contract, dependency or CLI behaviour changed.

body: The occupied-resources rule over test-private self-spawn markers, which names MCP_SERVE_TEST_CHILD as its precedent, is stale by omission: ROOT_TIED_TEST_CHILD and HARNESS_TIED_TEST_CHILD are new markers of the same kind.

Environment variables carry the VIOLA_ prefix, and the VIOLA_ namespace is product plumbing only. The two new markers stand outside VIOLA_ as test-only names that no viola build reads, the same exception the existing test-child marker holds.
Harness variables are never read by viola, and test seams are not a configuration channel. Each new marker is read only by its own test binary.
Root tests freeze a wrapper through one SIGSTOP guard. A frozen wrapper's survival of a killed test is now witnessed, and the frozen wrapper is tied like every other root spawn.

Test evidence survives a killed test, and test homes are removed by their owner record only. A killed test now leaves no booted wrapper or fake agent, and its victim writes its report under the witness's own test home.
Root test waits share one bound. The new wait that every recorded descendant is gone runs within that shared bound before it kills survivors.

Each test runs in its own viola home under the once-per-build shared verify stamp. The stamp now counts only by its completion file and ledger stamps file, and a hollow one gets a next-generation dir with nothing removed.

verify is the one stamps writer, and malformed or untrusted stamps read as unverified. The test stamp is still written only by a viola verify run, and that run is now tied when an in-test harness session stamps.
viola-e2e is test-only, and so is the viola-harness binary. The harness boot gains a tied option and two constructors: an in-test session ties its supervisor, and the CLI boot does not.

Test-only binaries are kept out of release builds, and the e2e crate's no-op fake-agent feature still holds. There are two new test binaries: a root cross_ end-to-end binary and a viola-e2e integration binary.
Indirect, through the tie helper: libc is the one OS-binding crate. The parent-death signal is set through libc prctl in a pre_exec hook, and no new crate was added.
Indirect, through the tie helper: process start time is read from the OS through sysinfo. The test process tree records each pid with its sysinfo start time, so only a matching survivor is killed.
Linux only, and OS-gated tests name their reason. The tie uses the Linux parent-death signal.
The zero-panics gate allows no panic line in end-to-end runs. The new panicked-test witness panics its victim on purpose, and the tree wait panics to name any survivor.
The real claude CLI runs only locally, and tests run against the fake agent. Every new witness boots the fake agent; no live claude was started.
Homes are kept after each job's end-to-end run. A stamp dir may now stand as viola-stamp-<key>-g<n> beside a hollow viola-stamp-<key> left as found.

Every long-lived viola child a root test spawns is tied to its spawning thread by a parent-death SIGKILL, and a census test holds that no root test spawns viola untied. An in-test harness session's supervisor and stamping verify are tied the same way, but the viola-harness CLI boot's supervisor is not.

The shared test verify stamp counts only when it holds its completion file and ledger stamps file. A hollow stamp is left standing, and the next generation is built under viola-stamp-<key>-g<n> through a temporary dir renamed into place. No stamp dir is removed.

body: decision/obs-deps-pass-cargo-deny, decision/cargo-deny-failure-fails and decision/ci-gates-fail-closed: the supply-chain job is red as-left on RUSTSEC-2026-0543, so an obs dependency no longer passes cargo deny; the session does not mend it and asks its remedy at route-resolve.

decision/direct-chrono-dependency: chrono, the direct timestamp dependency, is the crate the advisory names unmaintained; it stands four ways in the graph, so replacing its direct use would not remove it.
decision/rerun-no-substitute: the operator pass ruled out a re-run of the red supply-chain job as no remedy, the same reading the row holds for diagnostics.

decision/test-homes-under-e2e-home and decision/test-homes-under-scan-root: a stamped test home's base may now stand as a next-generation stamp dir with a completion file, and the killed-test victims write their pid report under the witness's own test home.

decision/homes-kept-until-gates-run and decision/test-homes-kept-until-gates: a hollow stamp is left as found and nothing is removed; a killed test no longer leaves a running wrapper writing into a kept home after the test ends.

decision/ci-verify-fake-agent-only and decision/real-cli-verify-never-in-ci: the stamping viola verify of an in-test harness session is now tied to the test, still against the fake agent.
decision/no-sleep-based-log-waits: the new witnesses wait for the victim's report and for the recorded processes to be gone within a bounded deadline, then SIGKILL survivors and fail.
decision/os-gated-test-census and decision/linux-only-os-target: the tie rests on the Linux parent-death signal, and the new witness binaries depend on it.

decision/env-vars-not-config-channel and decision/env-vars-not-configuration: two test-only self-spawn markers, ROOT_TIED_TEST_CHILD and HARNESS_TIED_TEST_CHILD, outside VIOLA_*, each read by its own test binary and by no viola build.

decision/gauges-from-harness-snapshots, decision/perf-job-runs-g2 and decision/hook-benchmark-on-passing-instance: the harness boot options the perf run and harness sessions build gained a tied flag; the perf boot names it with no change of behaviour.

body:
The session ties every long-lived viola child a root test spawns to its test: a pre_exec sets the parent-death signal to SIGKILL and exits when the recorded parent is gone, so a booted wrapper and its fake agent end with their test, killed or panicked.
An in-test harness session's supervisor and its stamping viola verify are tied the same way; the CLI boot of the test harness stays untied, unchanged in behaviour.
The shared verify stamp of the test homes counts only with a completion file and its stamps file; a hollow stamp restored without its files is left standing as found, nothing removed, and a next-generation stamp dir is built beside it.
A census test now finds no untied direct viola spawn under the root tests; it measured 45 sites, one more than research said, all moved behind the tie.
A test-side witness records the victim's process tree by pid and start time and, at its deadline, SIGKILLs only the recorded survivors whose pid and start time still match.
CI on the pushed commit read the test job green on an exact rust-cache restore with no cache deleted; the supply-chain job is red on a new unmaintained-crate advisory for chrono, not mended here, no ignore added and no re-run, its remedy asked of the overseer.

body:
The session ties every long-lived viola child a root test spawns to the spawning test thread (parent-death SIGKILL, and an exit when the recorded parent is already gone), so a SIGKILLed or panicked test leaves no wrapper or fake agent running.
45 direct root spawn sites of viola were moved onto one tied spawn builder; a new census test (with a planted positive) holds that no root test spawns viola untied, matching any path that ends in the VIOLA constant. The prior count of 44 sites in 24 files was disproved by one more spelling.
The harness boot options gain a tied flag and two constructors: an in-test harness session ties its supervisor and its stamping viola verify, while the CLI boot keeps its supervisor untied and unchanged in behaviour. The in-test boots of the harness lifecycle and harness CLI tests stay untied.
The shared verify stamp now counts only when it holds a completion file and its stamps file. A hollow stamp, such as one a CI cache restored without its files, is never trusted and nothing is removed: the next generation dir (viola-stamp-key-gN) is stamped through a temp dir renamed into place.
New witnesses: killed-test cases for piped, direct, outer-PTY and frozen wrappers, a panicked-test case, and a killed harness-session case, plus two hollow-stamp cases. At its deadline a witness SIGKILLs every recorded survivor whose pid and start time still match, then fails naming it. The CI 20 s stamped-home kill line now covers the killed-test witness binary.
No product code, dependency, manifest or CI workflow changed. CI's test job went green on an exact rust-cache restore. The supply-chain red (a new advisory) is not this session's, and no ignore was added.

decision/one-shared-test-helper and decision/shared-e2e-helpers: a new shared root helper (the tied spawn builder and the process-tree witness) is the one copy every root spawn site and witness uses.

decision/no-sleep-synchronization and decision/no-test-retries-or-sleeps: the new witnesses poll a bounded deadline on recorded processes. These rows rule over their waits.

body_fields.fact: Every long-lived viola child a root test spawns is tied to its spawning test thread by a parent-death SIGKILL (and exits when the recorded parent is already gone), so a SIGKILLed or panicked test leaves no wrapper or fake agent; the Drop guard still covers the normal end.
A census test holds that no root test spawns viola untied, matching any Command::new path equal to or ending in the VIOLA constant over every test source recursively, proven on a planted positive.
The parent-death signal follows the spawning thread, so a tied viola child is spawned only on a thread that outlives it.

A verify stamp counts only when it holds its completion file and its stamps file; a hollow stamp is never trusted and never removed, and the next generation dir viola-stamp-key-gN is stamped instead through a temp dir renamed into place, then reused without stamping again.

An in-test harness session ties its supervisor and its stamping viola verify to the test's thread; the agent-run CLI boot leaves its supervisor untied so it outlives boot; the in-test boots of the harness lifecycle and harness CLI tests are untied, a known gap.

A killed-test witness records the victim's process tree with start times, waits within WITHIN, then SIGKILLs every survivor whose pid and start time still match and fails naming each survivor by subject.
